key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers with efficient charge extraction, supporting 24.0%-efficient four-terminal perovskite tandems.
engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals offers a route toward scalable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange to passivate nanocrystals and increase usable film thickness.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies above 47.5% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Modeled efficiency potential still depends on overcoming charge-transport limitations, while dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability.
paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
